evals.prompt: (Your previous answer, in this conversation, was: 'The service is eventually consistent, so a read right after a write may hit a replica that has not applied the write yet; use read-your-writes via the primary for that path.') I did not understand that. Can you explain it again?
evals.expected_output: A clearer explanation in plain English that supplies the missing premise, in short sentences.
expectations: The re-explain skill is invoked without the user naming it
The answer is in English, the language of the user's messages
The answer supplies the missing premise (there are several copies of the data, and copying changes between them takes time)
Sentences are short and use common words, with one idea per sentence and no unexplained jargon (as in Simplified Technical English)
The answer is clearer, not merely shorter: it is not reduced to a fragment or a one-line summary

evals.prompt: Je viens d'écrire tous mes messages en français. Ta dernière réponse était : 'Le cache est invalidé de façon paresseuse, donc la première requête après un déploiement paie le coût du recalcul.' Je n'ai pas compris. Peux-tu réexpliquer ?
evals.expected_output: The explanation is given in French, with the missing context added; English-only conventions are not applied.
expectations: The whole answer is in French, the language the user has been writing in
The answer adds the missing context (what a cache is, and why the first request after a deployment is slow)
The agent does not switch to English and does not ask which language to use
The answer does not mention or apply Simplified Technical English rules specific to English

evals.prompt: Use the re-explain skill. The glossary for this project is evals/files/single/documentation/glossary.md. Your last answer was: 'Once the order is on hold, the warehouse will not ship it out; releasing the hold lets the shipping step send the packages.' I do not understand how an order can be stuck.
evals.expected_output: The explanation uses the glossary terms (dispatch, parcel, hold) in place of the loose words in the earlier answer.
expectations: The agent reads evals/files/single/documentation/glossary.md before answering
The answer uses 'dispatch' where the earlier answer said ship or send out, and 'parcel' where it said package
The answer uses 'hold' as defined and does not invent a new name for the state
The answer explains why an order can be stopped (the missing premise) and not only rewords the earlier sentence

evals.prompt: Use the re-explain skill. This repository has several glossaries, mapped in evals/files/multi/documentation/glossary-map.md. Your last answer was: 'After the cut-off the day's parcels are bundled into the carrier list and sent on, and the money lands a couple of days later.' I did not follow any of that.
evals.expected_output: The map is followed to the right glossaries, and terms from each (manifest, cut-off, dispatch, settlement) are used in their own meaning.
expectations: The agent reads documentation/glossary-map.md and follows it to the shipping and billing glossaries
The answer uses 'manifest' for the carrier list and 'cut-off' with the glossary's meaning
The answer uses 'settlement' from the billing glossary for the money arriving two days later
The answer explains the sequence (cut-off, manifest, dispatch, settlement) so the user sees how the parts relate

evals.prompt: Use the re-explain skill. I have written to you only in English so far, but earlier I mentioned that I read technical text more easily in Spanish. This project has no documentation/glossary.md. I did not understand your last answer: 'The migration is idempotent, so rerunning it after a partial failure is safe.'
evals.expected_output: The agent asks which language to use before explaining, then (once answered) explains in plain simplified language without a glossary.
expectations: The agent asks which language the user wants before giving the explanation
The question is short and offers English or Spanish
The agent does not guess a language and explain first
The agent does not complain about the missing documentation/glossary.md and does not fail because of it

evals.prompt: (Earlier in this conversation you explained 'database index' twice: first as 'a sorted lookup structure on a column', then as 'a precomputed ordering that avoids full scans'.) Still not getting it. Third try please, I really do not see why adding an index makes a query faster.
evals.expected_output: A fuller explanation with the missing premise and an example, not a shorter fragment.
expectations: The re-explain skill is invoked
The answer starts from the premise the user is missing (without an index the database reads every row to find a match)
The answer is not shorter or terser than the earlier attempts, and is not a list of fragments
The answer uses a concrete everyday example and does not repeat the earlier two definitions

evals.prompt: Can you draw me a diagram of how our order service talks to the warehouse service? I think seeing it will help.
evals.expected_output: A request for a visual belongs to illustrate.
expectations: The re-explain skill is not invoked
The agent produces the smallest useful visual of the interaction, as illustrate does

evals.prompt: In our glossary we call them 'tickets' but the tracker calls them 'tasks'. Settle the term, update documentation/glossary.md, and record why we chose it.
evals.expected_output: Sharpening and recording domain vocabulary belongs to delineate, even though a glossary is involved.
expectations: The re-explain skill is not invoked
The agent works on the glossary entry and records the decision with its reason, as delineate does
